title: Abolitionism
notes: Cited for: Many Northerners distrusted abolitionists, who threatened harmony between North and South and ran counter to a Constitution that left slavery to the states.

title: Compromise of 1850
notes: Cited for: Terms; the Fugitive Slave Act turned many moderate Northerners into opponents of slavery extension.

title: Cotton gin
notes: Cited for: Invented by Whitney in 1793; wire teeth on a revolving cylinder; fixed cotton in the South and institutionalized slavery.

title: Elijah P. Lovejoy
notes: Cited for: Antislavery editor; press destroyed by mobs; killed defending it at Alton, Illinois, November 7, 1837.

title: Erie Canal
notes: Cited for: Finished 1825; linked the Great Lakes to New York City via the Hudson at Albany; made New York City a major commercial center.

title: Frederick Douglass
notes: Cited for: Escaped September 1838 disguised as a sailor; Narrative 1845; The North Star 1847; attended Seneca Falls.

title: Great Famine (Irish history)
notes: Cited for: Blight arrived 1845; about one million died; perhaps 2 million more emigrated.

title: Know-Nothing party
notes: Cited for: Anti-immigrant, anti-Catholic party of the 1850s targeting Irish and German immigrants; origin of the name; longer wait for citizenship.

title: Manifest Destiny
notes: Cited for: O'Sullivan's 1845 phrase; divinely ordained expansion; Whig opposition as belligerent and arrogant.

title: Nat Turner
notes: Cited for: August 1831 revolt in Virginia; 55 to 60 white people killed; at least 100 Black people killed in suppression; Turner hanged; new laws on education, movement and assembly.

title: Seneca Falls Convention
notes: Cited for: July 19 to 20, 1848; Mott and Stanton barred in London in 1840; declaration modeled on the Declaration of Independence; voting resolution the only one not unanimous; 68 women and 32 men signed.

title: Underground Railroad
notes: Cited for: Secret network; railway terms such as stations and conductors; Tubman as conductor.

title: William Lloyd Garrison
notes: Cited for: The Liberator first issue January 1, 1831; immediatism; American Anti-Slavery Society 1833.

title: Worcester v. Georgia
notes: Cited for: March 3, 1832 ruling that Georgia law had no force in the Cherokee Nation; Georgia ignored it and Jackson declined to enforce it.

title: Lincoln's Spot Resolution
publisher: US House of Representatives: History, Art & Archives
notes: Cited for: December 1847 resolution protesting the war and asking whether the spot where blood was shed was US soil.

title: Courtship and Marriage (Hidden Voices: Enslaved Women in the Lowcountry and U.S. South)
publisher: Lowcountry Digital History Initiative, College of Charleston
notes: Cited for: Southern laws refused to recognize enslaved marriages; communities took them seriously; jumping the broom; spouses separated by sale.

title: Cherokee Phoenix (New Echota [Ga.]) 1828-1829
notes: Cited for: Cherokee Phoenix first issue 1828 at New Echota, printed with Sequoyah’s 86-character syllabary (1821).

title: Compromise of 1850
notes: Cited for: California free; Utah and New Mexico territories; DC slave trade ended; stricter Fugitive Slave Act; Clay and Douglas.

title: Eli Whitney's Patent for the Cotton Gin
notes: Cited for: Sticky-seeded inland cotton; the gin raised demand for land and enslaved labor; 1808 ban on the African trade; ever-larger, more regimented plantations.

title: Diseños: An Impact of Mexican Cession
notes: Cited for: 1851 law required Mexican landowners in California to confirm titles; the cost was often the land itself.

title: Kansas-Nebraska Act (1854)
notes: Cited for: Douglas bill; popular sovereignty; repealed the Missouri Compromise; passed May 30, 1854; Bleeding Kansas.

title: Missouri Compromise (1820)
notes: Cited for: Missouri slave, Maine free, to keep the balance; slavery barred north of 36°30′; repealed 1854.

title: Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo (1848)
notes: Cited for: Signed February 2, 1848; Mexico ceded 55 percent of its territory; $15 million; Mexicans could stay and keep their property.

title: African American Christianity, Pt. I: To the Civil War
notes: Cited for: Obedience preaching; hush harbors called by signals and passwords; African rhythms mixed with evangelical Christianity; double meanings of spirituals.

title: The Slave Trade (Many Voices, One Nation)
publisher: National Museum of American History, Smithsonian
notes: Cited for: Internal slave trade forced up to a million enslaved people from the Upper South to Deep South cotton plantations.

title: Declaration of Sentiments
notes: Cited for: Full text: "all men and women are created equal"; elective franchise; "civilly dead"; wages she earns.

title: Erie Canalway National Heritage Corridor: History & Culture
notes: Cited for: Canal in operation since 1825; made New York the premier commercial center; opened the interior to settlement.

title: Visit Forks of the Road
notes: Cited for: Tens of thousands brought in chains from Virginia, Maryland, Kentucky and the Carolinas to the Natchez market.

title: Harriet Tubman
notes: Cited for: Escaped 1849 when about to be sold; about 13 trips into Maryland; said she never lost a passenger.

title: House Divided Speech
notes: Cited for: Full text of Lincoln’s June 16, 1858 speech at Springfield, Illinois.

title: The Mill Girls of Lowell
notes: Cited for: Young Yankee women 15 to 30 recruited from farms; cash wages, boardinghouses, 12 to 14 hour days; early protests as "daughters of freemen".

title: Lucretia Mott
notes: Cited for: Mott and Stanton met at the 1840 World Anti-Slavery Convention in London, where women were excluded, and agreed to hold a convention; held July 19 and 20, 1848.

title: Resisting Slavery
notes: Cited for: Everyday resistance: slowing work, pretending to be sick, breaking tools.

title: Report of the Woman's Rights Convention
notes: Cited for: Elective franchise resolution; 68 women and 32 men signed; Douglass spoke in support of the cause of woman.

title: History & Culture - Trail Of Tears National Historic Trail
notes: Cited for: Removal Act 1830; Treaty of New Echota by a small faction, ratified 1836; 1838 army removal of more than 16,000 Cherokee; other Southeastern nations relocated; the Cherokee rebuilt.

title: What Happened on the Trail of Tears
notes: Cited for: Sequoyah syllabary and written constitution; New Echota signers not elected officials; Elizur Butler estimated over 4,000 deaths.

title: What is the Underground Railroad?
notes: Cited for: Self-emancipation, often unaided; helpers of all races; destinations including Canada, Mexico and Spanish Florida.

title: Oregon Territory, 1846
publisher: Office of the Historian, US Department of State
notes: Cited for: Oregon Trail migration; 1846 treaty with Britain extending the border along the 49th parallel.

title: The Annexation of Texas, the Mexican-American War, and the Treaty of Guadalupe-Hidalgo, 1845-1848
publisher: Office of the Historian, US Department of State
notes: Cited for: Texas independence 1836, admitted December 29, 1845; Nueces vs Rio Grande border dispute; war declared May 13, 1846; 525,000 square miles ceded for $15 million; Wilmot Proviso.

notes: Cited for: Quotes the first Liberator: "I WILL BE HEARD"; immediate emancipation unpopular even among Northern antislavery advocates.

title: Lowell Mill Girls
notes: Cited for: Turnouts of 1834 (wage cut) and 1836 (higher board).

notes: Cited for: Irish settled in Northeastern cities; all Irish and many Germans were Catholic; Know Nothings anti-Catholic.
